chapter_title: AI Guardrails: Teaching Thinking Without Over-Reliance
learning_objective: The learner will examine a table of pass probabilities for five mastery rules and select the rule or rules that meet each of four stated requirements, correctly answering at least three of four.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** mastery-threshold-chooser
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze
**Bloom Verb:** examine
**Learning Objective:** The learner will examine a table of pass probabilities for five mastery rules and select the rule or rules that meet each of four stated requirements, correctly answering at least three of four. **Prerequisites:** mastery threshold, false pass, false fail, pass probability (all defined in the section "The Mastery Threshold" above). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of 4 requirements, the learner selects every rule that meets it and submits. A selection is correct when it equals the "Correct rules" set in Content exactly, with no missing and no extra rules. Mastery is 3 of 4 correct on the first attempt. Reading the table is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A stricter rule is always better. (2) "Four of five" is a high standard. (3) A rule that never passes a weak student also passes every strong one. **Instructional Rationale:** Selecting rules that satisfy two requirements at once forces the learner to read across the table for several students and see the trade-off between false passes and false fails. Requirements with one answer, two answers, and a single strict answer show that the best rule depends on what the school values. **Content:** The table of pass probabilities, shown in full (a student passes when they meet the rule on a fresh set of questions): | Rule | Student at 50% | Student at 70% | Student at 90% | |---|---|---|---| | 4 of 5 | 18.8% | 52.8% | 91.9% | | 5 of 5 | 3.1% | 16.8% | 59.0% | | 8 of 10 | 5.5% | 38.3% | 93.0% | | 9 of 10 | 1.1% | 14.9% | 73.6% | | 10 of 10 | 0.1% | 2.8% | 34.9% | Four requirements: | # | Requirement shown to the learner | Correct rules | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | A student at 70% should pass less than 20% of the time, and a student at 90% should pass at least 70% of the time. | 9 of 10 | 9 of 10 passes the 70% student 14.9% of the time and the 90% student 73.6%; 5 of 5 and 10 of 10 fail the second condition, and the others fail the first. | | 2 | A student at 90% should pass at least 90% of the time. | 4 of 5; 8 of 10 | These two pass the 90% student 91.9% and 93.0% of the time; the others pass less often. | | 3 | A student at 50% should pass less than 1% of the time. | 10 of 10 | Only 10 of 10, at 0.1%, is below 1%; 9 of 10 is 1.1%. | | 4 | A student at 70% should pass less than 50% of the time, and a student at 90% should pass at least 90% of the time. | 8 of 10 | 8 of 10 passes the 70% student 38.3% and the 90% student 93.0%; 4 of 5 passes the 70% student 52.8%. | **Provenance:** The pass probabilities are computed from the binomial distribution for the stated true accuracies and are shown to one decimal place; the sim must show the formula or label them "Computed values." The accuracy levels are illustrative. **Rules:** The set for each requirement is the set of rules whose probabilities satisfy every stated condition, using the comparisons exactly as written (< and >=). A requirement is scored on its first submitted set only. The score counts first-attempt correct sets out of 4. Mastery is a score >= 3. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees the table and one requirement at a time. 2. The learner selects every rule that meets the requirement and submits it. The sim marks it correct or incorrect and shows the feedback text. 3. If incorrect, the learner may select again; the second attempt does not change the score. After the second attempt, the correct set and reason are shown. 4. After all 4 requirements, the sim shows the score. 5. The learner should notice that no rule is best for every requirement. **Feedback:** 4 requirements, fixed order, two attempts each. Correct: "Correct. [Why text]." Incorrect: "Not quite. Check each stated condition in the table for every rule." After the second attempt the correct set is revealed and the requirement counts as missed. A running score "First-try correct: n of 4" is shown. Final message for a score >= 3: "You can choose a rule to fit the need." For a score < 3: "Reread the table and try again." **Starting State:** The full table is shown with requirement 1, no rule selected, and the prompt "Which rules meet this requirement?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's table has five rules and three accuracy levels with the same values. The chapter states that "four of five" passes a student at 70 percent about 53 percent of the time. The mastery bar is 3 of 4.
